eli5.text: When you open the app today and go to the home page, the video now plays in a pop-up window instead of sitting right on the page, and the text under the title is shorter. The team also added a couple of new quotes from users you can read, made the free plan clearly labeled as free for people who are signed in, and removed a feature that searched cryptocurrency market data from Manifold. Behind the scenes, a few file names and settings were changed from an old name to the current one.

ai.title: Extra knowledge updates no longer wrapped in XML tags
ai.summary: The `extra_knowledge_updates` XML tags were removed from the main prompt response in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. The content now uses a plain text header `I'll also update the following knowledge:` followed directly by the file blocks. This change affects how the agent surfaces knowledge updates in its responses.

eli5.text: When the assistant decides to share some helpful knowledge updates alongside its main reply, that side content used to be tucked inside invisible XML-style markers. Now, instead of wrapping the updates in those technical markers, the assistant simply adds a plain English header that reads "I'll also update the following knowledge:" right before listing the files. For anyone watching how the assistant presents these updates, the visible result is the same helpful list of files; the only difference is the assistant no longer surrounds that list with the XML-style tags that were never meant to be seen. This adjustment is live as of today and affects only how these knowledge updates are formatted in the assistant's responses.

ai.title: Add startup log to Express app
ai.summary: Added console.log statement to Express app initialization in test mock project. Provides startup visibility for Manifold API server.

eli5.text: When the Manifold API server starts up, it now prints a single line to the system log indicating it is beginning operation. This gives operators a visible signal that the server is initializing, rather than starting silently. The change applies only to the internal test mock of the API project, so it does not affect the live system today.

ai.title: aider added to .gitignore
ai.summary: Added `.aider*` to `.gitignore`. Prevents aider editor artifacts from being tracked in the repository. Scope limited to the root `.gitignore` file.

eli5.text: The project's ignore list now includes a specific set of temporary files created by an AI coding helper, so those helper files won't accidentally get saved alongside the main code. This only affects developers working on the project's codebase, if you're not editing the code yourself, you won't notice anything different. It's a small cleanup step that keeps the shared code folder tidy and prevents stray helper files from cluttering the project.

ai.title: Remove code block extraction in process-file-block
ai.summary: Deleted regex-based code block extraction logic from `backend/src/process-file-block.ts`. The function now returns raw response content directly instead of attempting to parse Markdown fences. This simplifies the post-processing step for file generation.

eli5.text: The assistant no longer strips out Markdown code fences (like triple backticks) from its text replies when saving generated files; it pastes the raw reply content directly into the file instead. This affects the behind-the-scenes file-generation step that turns assistant responses into saved documents. If you looked at the saved files today, you might see leftover backtick markers or formatting artifacts around code snippets that were previously cleaned out automatically.

ai.title: main-prompt.ts: readFilesPaths only from newFiles
ai.summary: Changed readFilesPaths in getFileVersionUpdates to use only newFiles, excluding previousFilePaths. This restricts the file reading logic to newly added files. Scope is limited to backend/src/main-prompt.ts.

eli5.text: The system now only reads newly added files instead of also re-reading previously processed ones. This affects the backend service that tracks file versions. If you watched the system work, you'd see it skip over files it had already looked at in past runs.

ai.title: Add FAQ section to home page
ai.summary: Introduced a new FAQ section to the main landing page, rendering a list of common questions and answers using native HTML details/summary elements for collapsible interaction. The content is sourced from a new web/src/lib/faq.tsx file, which exports a typed array of question/answer objects. This change adds web/src/lib/faq.tsx and modifies web/src/app/page.tsx to import and render the faqs array within a new section.

eli5.text: The home page now shows a frequently asked questions section, so visitors can click on a question and see the answer expand right below it without leaving the page. The answers live in a single list that the home page pulls in and displays, which is why the page needed new code to arrange and render each one as a collapsible item. If you scrolled to the bottom of the home page today, you'd see a new 'FAQ' heading followed by questions like 'Do you store my data?' and 'What models do you use?' that open on a click.

ai.title: Switch to git-style SEARCH/REPLACE diff blocks
ai.summary: System prompts and file utilities now enforce git-style `<<<<<<< SEARCH` / `>>>>>>> REPLACE` markers instead of XML-like `<search>` / `<replace>` tags. A new `createSearchReplaceBlock` helper in `common/src/util/file.ts` generates these standardized blocks, which `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` uses to construct examples. This aligns the AI's output format with familiar git diff syntax for better parsing consistency.

eli5.text: From today, when the assistant suggests changes to a file, it now wraps the before-and-after snippets in the familiar git-style merge markers (the same conflict dividers you see in code reviews), replacing the older angle-bracket <search>/<replace> tags. If you ever read one of these change suggestions, you'll now spot the classic <<<<<<< SEARCH... =======... >>>>>>> REPLACE blocks instead of the old XML-looking tags, making the proposed edits easier to scan for anyone used to git. The assistant still does the same job of proposing file edits; only the container format of those edit snippets changed.

ai.title: Version bump 1.0.104
ai.summary: Bump `codebuff` package version to 1.0.104. Internal release housekeeping. Scope: `npm-app/package.json`.

eli5.text: The assistant's version label was bumped to 1.0.104. This release lets the assistant switch to git-style search and replace markers when editing code, and adds a new FAQ section to the home page that you can expand and collapse. It also includes several behind-the-scenes updates, like removing XML tags from knowledge updates and adding a startup log, but those are internal changes. The new version is available today.
